title: A Giant Stone Clock Accurate to 2 Seconds
description: In the 1700s, Jaipur built a sundial 27 metres tall. How Jantar Mantar measured time and the sky without a telescope.

scenes.narration: Nearly three hundred years ago, India built a clock out of stone, as tall as a nine-storey building.
scenes.image_prompt: a huge triangular stone sundial wall rising high into a clear sky, 18th century Jaipur, people small at its base, bright sun

scenes.narration: It's the 1730s in Jaipur. Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh the Second is obsessed with the sky.
scenes.image_prompt: 18th century Rajput maharaja in fine robes and turban studying star charts and brass astronomical instruments in a palace room

scenes.narration: He builds Jantar Mantar, a yard of giant instruments made of stone and marble.
scenes.image_prompt: wide view of an open courtyard filled with giant geometric stone astronomical instruments, curved ramps and circular structures, Jaipur

scenes.narration: The biggest, the Samrat Yantra, is a sundial about twenty-seven metres tall.
scenes.image_prompt: the Samrat Yantra sundial at Jaipur, a massive staircase-like triangular gnomon with curved quadrant scales on both sides

scenes.narration: Its shadow moves across the marked scale fast enough to read local time to about two seconds.
scenes.image_prompt: close up of a sharp shadow edge moving across finely engraved marble time markings on a giant sundial, an astronomer watching

scenes.narration: Other instruments track stars, planets and the sun's path through the year, all by eye.
scenes.image_prompt: astronomers at night using a large bowl-shaped sunken stone instrument with markings to sight stars, starry sky above

scenes.narration: He built similar observatories in other cities too, including Delhi.
scenes.image_prompt: red sandstone astronomical instruments of an 18th century observatory in Delhi, tall curved walls and a central gnomon, morning light

scenes.narration: Jaipur's Jantar Mantar is now a UNESCO site, and the sundial still works. Follow for more lost tech.
scenes.image_prompt: present day Jantar Mantar Jaipur with visitors walking among the giant instruments, Nahargarh hills behind, golden hour
